lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality.
items.because: These personal details direct attention away from qualifications.

items.says: Education appears before the more relevant product internship.
items.because: Putting Experience first would show product work before the MBA.

items.says: The hospital practicum takes space from more relevant product experience.
items.because: Its healthcare work is distinct from the app venture’s product work.

items.says: No post-MBA employment is listed after June 2025.
There is an eight-month interval between the degree and the first listed role.
The 35% conversion improvement lacks a baseline and does not distinguish a relative increase from a percentage-point change.
items.because: The two measures mean different things, so readers cannot judge the improvement.

items.says: The dispute self-service bullet says the team shipped early but not what the feature changed.
The early-shipping result is buried after the alignment detail.
The roadmap consequence appears only at the end of the chargeback bullet.
The written-out dollar amount uses unnecessary space.
The onboarding comparison gives a method but no finding or decision it informed.
items.because: Without one, the value of the comparison remains unclear.

items.says: The bullet wrongly attributes the 9-to-4-day difference to the redesign.
items.because: Merchants opted into the new flow, so differences between the groups could affect payment timing.

items.says: The opt-in comparison is not an A/B test and cannot substantiate the A/B-testing claim.
items.because: An A/B test requires randomized assignment, while merchants choosing a flow may differ beforehand.

items.says: “Cut late deliveries” wrongly presents a calculation change as an operational improvement.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the reported rate, not whether shipments arrived late.

items.says: “Cut warehouse pick errors 30%” is missing “by.”
items.because: Without it, the result reads as an unfinished construction.

items.says: “Prepares” is the wrong tense for a role that ended.
items.because: The rest of the bullet describes past work, and the role ended in August 2023.

items.says: The S&OP bullet does not say what the review changed.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it informed a planning decision or improved a forecast.

items.says: Preparing the forecast pack does not show the analytical contribution behind it.
“For each meeting” repeats the quarterly-review context.
The driver-hours saving is buried after rollout and training details.
items.because: It is the clearest consequence of the work, but a scanning reader encounters it last.

items.says: The strongest route-planning bullet does not open the entry.
items.because: Opening with the late-delivery calculation gives a weaker and misleading first impression.

items.says: The wording blurs whether the dining halls were users or partners.
The description of food otherwise discarded is longer than needed.
Weekly active-user growth does not show whether reminders reduced missed pickups.
Consecutive bullets opening with “Launched” make the actions less distinct.
“Volunteer shift system” does not identify what kind of system was introduced.
“Staff cover shifts” does not say what staff had to cover.
The bullet expresses the same weekly time unit two different ways.
The scheduling bullet describes meetings but not a scheduling result.
items.because: Meeting frequency does not show whether the sessions produced a decision, recommendation or improvement.

items.says: The scheduling bullet leads with meeting activity rather than your contribution.
items.because: The topic and Team Lead title do not identify the work you led.

items.says: The clinic-intake change is not the practicum’s opening bullet.
items.because: It gives more concrete evidence than the opening description of meetings.

items.says: Passive voice hides your actions on patient intake.
items.because: The sentence says what happened but not directly who did the work.

items.says: The bullet states staff adoption but not the benefit of the shorter intake form.
The adoption result is buried, and “the changes” does not name what staff adopted.
The merchant-payment result is wrongly placed under the hospital practicum and repeats the payments-internship achievement.
items.because: Merchant onboarding and the 2,300-merchant figure belong to the payments internship, making the project attribution doubtful.

items.says: “By redesigning onboarding” does not identify the process change.
items.because: It gives little evidence of the work behind the outcome.

items.says: The phrase describing time to first payment is unnecessarily long.
items.because: Its length obscures a metric that can be named directly.
